definition: MADD stands for multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency, a rare inherited metabolic disorder passed down in an autosomal recessive pattern. It is caused by changes in the ETFA, ETFB, or ETFDH genes that lead to deficiency in electron transfer flavoprotein or its dehydrogenase, and it can involve physical abnormalities, low muscle tone, heart enlargement, liver enlargement, metabolic acidosis, low blood sugar, and behavioral changes.
